#4504. BYD’s 300-MPH Electric Hypercar Crashed During Testing. The Driver Survived

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Making the world’s fastest car comes with bragging rights, but that doesn’t mean much if safety is put second. Thankfully, that doesn’t seem to be the case with BYD’s Yangwang U9 Extreme, a Chinese-made electric hypercar that made headlines last year when it broke the 300 miles per hour barrier, securing its place among automotive royalty.

The world’s fastest car crashed hard during what looks like high-speed testing, but the driver reportedly walked out on his own without severe injuries, according to CarNewsChina. That can’t be said for the car, though. After hitting a barrier at an undisclosed speed, the two-door hypercar’s front and rear sections disintegrated, leaving just the central passenger compartment relatively intact. There were no reported battery fires.

BYD claims the U9 Extreme’s safety structure is based on a carbon fiber passenger cell designed to provide high torsional rigidity and protection in a crash. The automaker didn’t say when and where the crash occurred, but it was likely during a new speed record attempt.

In September 2025, the 2,977-horsepower hypercar hit 308.4 miles per hour (496.22 kilometers per hour), surpassing big names like Bugatti, Rimac, and Koenigsegg. But the title of fastest car in the world apparently isn’t enough for the Chinese automaker, with BYD setting its sights on the 500 kph (310.6 mph) target.

The potential run was confirmed by Stella Li, BYD’s executive vice president, who seemed confident that the mind-boggling speed is achievable in its road-going, limited-run EV. After last year’s record run, the test driver said that he could have kept his foot on the throttle for another second and a half longer, according to the data. Whether or not that would be enough to squeeze an extra 2 mph is anyone’s guess, but there’s no denying that BYD tried.

Now, it’s unclear what will happen with the automaker’s record ambitions. Just 30 units of the Yangwang U9 Extreme are scheduled to be built, and with one out of the picture, a new attempt at hitting 310 mph might be delayed.

As its name suggests, the Extreme is the most outrageous version of the U9 supercar. Sporting a 1,200-volt electrical system, Yangwang’s headline-making two-door sports car has four electric motors and a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery with a 30C discharge rate. Titanium calipers and carbon-ceramic rotors help slow down the EV, helped by a set of GitiSport e-GTR2 Pro semi-slick tires that were specifically developed for speeds of up to 310.6 mph.

#4502. The Honda CR-V Has A Visibility Problem That Shouldn't Exist In 2026

Even some of the most popular, highly regarded cars in the world have their quirks. We found out that much with the latest Toyota RAV4, which has a center console design that many owners have found compromises comfort. It turns out that the Honda CR-V, the RAV4’s fiercest rival, has an unusual pain point of its own. The best-selling SUV in the U.S. this year so far, numerous CR-V owners have uncovered flaws in the Honda’s windshield wiper design. One would imagine that getting a wiper design wrong in 2026 is near impossible, but a lot of CR-V owners have been left frustrated by the wiper system’s inability to properly clean the windshield.

There are two separate issues with the CR-V’s wiper design, both of which have been spoken about at length on several social media forums. We also found complaints listed on the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) website.

The first issue involves the placement of the wiper system spray nozzles, which are situated on the wiper arms themselves. Many owners have found that when attempting to clean the windshield, the nozzles only begin spraying water when the wiper blades are roughly halfway up the windshield. As a result, many owners have complained that it’s not possible to properly clean the windshield, particularly in snowy or icy conditions, where hood-mounted nozzles would be more practical and better able to disperse the water.

“I will die on this hill. The wipers (especially when I’m using them w/windshield wiper fluid) are my ONLY gripe about this car. The design is terrible,” said one owner on Reddit.

“Having the windshield wiper fluid come out of the blades rather than spraying directly onto the windshield is useless as the fluid comes out while the wipers are half way up and fluid then gets pushed off the windshield and flows down the driver’s side window again affecting the driver’s visibility,” said another owner of a 2023 CR-V, who is based in Connecticut. This owner shared their experience on the NHTSA’s website.

These wiper-mounted nozzles are meant to eliminate the wind deflection or blind spots created by traditional, hood-mounted nozzles, but it appears that the current CR-V’s nozzles have not been properly engineered.

The second issue involves the driver’s-side wiper, which several owners say does not reach the edge of the windshield on the left. This leaves a significant portion of the windshield covered in dirt, creating another visibility concern. Some owners say the wipers only work properly if the vehicle is in Accessory Mode, while others were told by dealerships that the gap left on the driver’s side is normal.

“While driving my 2025 Hybrid CRV with 4K miles in a light rain, the wiper stopped going all the way to the edge and now only goes 90% of the way up no matter the setting. In a heavy rain, it will go 96%, and in accessory mode it goes up 100% of the way,” said an owner of a 2025 CR-V on Reddit. Other owners in the thread reported the same issue, with many filing complaints with the NHTSA and hoping for a recall. After all, visibility-related safety defects are often considered serious enough to initiate a recall.

A video posted by another Reddit user shows that an unacceptably large portion of the CR-V’s windshield isn’t reached by the left wiper blade, with a few commenters suggesting that it’s a software issue, not a mechanical alignment problem.

How to change wiper blades and washer fluid | Autoblog Wrenched

Manufacturers have invested heavily in technologies that enhance driver visibility, from blind-spot monitoring systems to surround-view monitors and pedestrian detection systems. But all of that doesn’t mean much if one of the most basic safety features, the windshield wiper, doesn’t do its job properly. At the very least, the performance of the current CR-V’s windshield wipers are inconsistent from one model to the next. While no recall has been issued for this condition and windshield wiper testing does not form part of safety tests run by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, that does not mean there isn’t a genuine concern. As visibility impacts overall safety, we would like to see Honda address the concern.

I find BMW’s Neue Klasse era to be a bit overwhelming, so I kept things simple with my 3-series. Though the 437-hp six-cylinder M350 is tempting, the 255-hp four-cylinder 330 offers enough power for my needs, and I like that it’s available in a standard rear-wheel-drive configuration. Given that the new 3 is larger and heavier than ever, I’ll consider this to be the “superleggera” spec.

The same goes for the $2000 M Sport package, M-tuned adaptive suspension ($550), and spare tire ($250 is worth the peace of mind of not getting stranded with an inflator kit).

Inside, I made the risky decision to pick the Digital White theme. I don’t have kids, but I’d definitely be enforcing a strict “No Flamin’ Hot Cheetos” rule. #4500. Mercedes-Benz Is Giving Up On Its EV Charging Network In Europe

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Mercedes-Benz has exited the EV charging market in Europe, selling its network to French operator Electra. The move was disclosed in the automaker’s third-quarter financial report, where the German brand said that the assets associated with the business were valued at €99 million ($111 million).

The sale, first reported by Electrive, means that Mercedes-Benz will now rely on external partnerships for EV charging exclusively in Europe. The car manufacturer’s proprietary EV network had 374 fast-charging ports at 47 locations across the region, all of which are now part of Electra’s growing network.

As part of the transaction, Electra is now a “Premium Partner,” second only to Ionity. What’s more, Mercedes-Benz EV drivers can now charge at discounted rates at over 5,000 Electra chargers across 800 locations in several European countries.

The German automaker’s fast charging business in the United States is unaffected by the European sale. That said, the move shows that Mercedes-Benz is no longer willing to invest its own money into building a premium charging experience. Instead, it’s relying on big partners like Ionity, which is already one of the best-performing networks in Europe.

One reason for the sale may be economies of scale. Paul Tonini, Electra’s General Manager for Germany, told Electrive that the market is increasingly consolidating around larger providers, which means that relatively small players like the now-defunct Mercedes-Benz Charging Network in Europe have a hard time keeping finances in check.

The bigger the network, the larger the potential for income. Meanwhile, Mercedes-Benz gets premium access to the network it used to operate, as it looks to expand its partnerships with third-party providers, offering EV owners discounted rates at more than one network.

The Mercedes-Benz Charging Network launched just three years ago, with a goal of having over 10,000 fast chargers globally by the end of the decade. The company uses high-powered charging equipment from Alpitronic, with the majority of sites having 400-kilowatt dispensers. Earlier this year, the first 1,000-kilowatt-capable stalls were installed at charging parks in Europe and North America.

This past weekend, the former Mercedes-Benz stalls have been integrated into Electra’s network. The card payment terminals will be replaced soon, and the station branding will also be changed to reflect Electra’s ownership.

In the United States, Mercedes-Benz’s High-Power Charging network has 748 charging ports at 80 locations, according to the Department of Energy’s Alternative Fuels Data Center. Additionally, 62 ports at eight stations are available in Canada.

#4499. Toyota’s Corolla Cross EV spotted for the first time [Images]

Toyota is giving its best-selling Corolla a major makeover, and an all-electric version is part of the plan. The upcoming Corolla Cross EV was captured in public for the first time ahead of its expected 2027 debut.

The Corolla has always been “a car for everyone,” Toyota’s former president and current CEO, Koji Sato, said after unveiling the next-gen Corolla Concept at last year’s Japan Mobility Show.

Since it went on sale 60 years ago, over 57 million drivers have chosen the Corolla, making it Toyota’s best-selling vehicle ever.

The Corolla has undergone 12 model changes since 1966, but the compact car is about to undergo its biggest transformation yet.

Although it’s still a top seller, the Corolla has lost some of its appeal as new, more advanced, and efficient options have emerged. Toyota looks to change that with the next-generation model.

It will remain “a car for everyone,” as Sato said, but the next-gen Corolla will come in multiple powertrains, including an all-electric version.

“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle―whatever the power source―let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive,” Sato said at the Japan Mobility Show last October.

Ahead of its expected debut sometime in 2027, a disguised Corolla Cross EV was spotted driving near Toyota’s European headquarters and R&D center.

New images from Chinese media outlet Autohome show what’s expected to be the all-electric Corolla Cross, with a closed-off grille and a unique body design.

The new Corolla will be the first to use Toyota’s new “multipathway” platform that will support electric, hybrid, gas, and other powertrains.

Toyota hasn’t revealed specifics, including battery or powertrain specs, but the next-gen Corolla EV is expected to remain close in style to the Concept. Aside from the massive COROLLA badge on the back, it looks like an entirely different vehicle with a near sports-car-like silhouette.

In an exclusive interview with Japanese media NHK in July, Toyota’s current chairman and former CEO, Akio Toyoda, warned that the company “cannot survive” if it does not adapt amid new competition and technology from China.

During the special, which went behind the scenes at Toyota’s “top secret” development site, several blurred Corolla Concept body types, including a sedan, hatchback, crossover, and GR model, were revealed in the background.

According to a recent Nikkei report, Toyota plans to begin production of the next-gen Corolla in 2028 through its joint venture with Chinese state-owned FAW Group, FAW Toyota Motor.

The Toyota Corolla EV is expected to be available in single- and dual-motor configurations with a driving range of at least 250 miles.

Let's hope that Toyota gets the Corolla EV right, because if it offers the right range for the right price but still feels fundamentally like a Corolla it is an EV that would get consideration from buyers who wouldn't otherwise consider an EV.

They're the buyers that trust Toyota and who consider the Corolla to be a nice safe choice for a car. And by safe, that means a vehicle that may not be all that exciting, but also a vehicle that they won't regret buying. Needless to say, these are not people who read Electrek, or even Car & Driver, for that matter. But there's a lot more of them than there are of us.

The hybrid version will reportedly use a new 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an electric motor. Toyota’s engineers told Car and Driver the system would deliver around 134 horsepower. It’s also estimated to be 10% to 20% more efficient than the current Corolla.

Toyota has yet to confirm the electric version will launch in the US. According to Car and Driver, the gas version will likely start at around $25,000, the hybrid around $27,000, and the EV and PHEVs will likely be priced in the $30,000 range.

#4498. An Uncompromising Fraternal Twin: We Drive the All-Electric 2027 BMW i3

It may not look all that different, but the electric i3 sedan differs from its 3-series siblings in a few key ways.

While BMW’s latest i3 may look like a carbon copy of its gas-powered 3-series sibling, using the gasser to underpin the EV would incur all manner of compromise. BMW did this with its i4 and the 430i models, and the concessions are obvious. In order to get a battery-electric powertrain tucked in the 430i’s body, BMW had to limit the battery size while using air springs to manage the car’s newfound mass. BMW wasn’t willing to make those sacrifices for its electric 3, and as a result, the i3 is actually quite different from its internal-combustion sibling.

The Munich-built BMW i3 50 xDrive sedan shares nothing with the new Dingolfing-made M350 and 330 models, except the front grille, the mirror housings, and possibly the door handles. Everything else is different, and that is reflected by a 1.5-inch stretch in wheelbase, plus some extra height and width. The length, on the other hand, differs only by a few hairs. But the difference is so much more than numbers on a page. Without having to worry about fitting an inline-six under the hood, the i3’s cabin is pushed forward, and the windshield glass picks up some extra rake. The Neue Klasse styling applied to both cars is effective at hiding these differences, but keen eyes may still pick up on the slightly steeper hood and the shorter front-wheel-to-door-edge gap.

See all results for new 2027 BMW i3 for sale near 33437

Adjusting the wheelbase and vehicle height was necessary to fit the electric drivetrain BMW wanted in there, and as a result, we think the i3 50 xDrive outshines the i4. The prime mover is a current-excited synchronous rear motor making 322 horsepower and 321 pound-feet of torque, the same kind of e-motor in the i4. However, the i3’s front motor has been changed to a 165-hp, 188-lb-ft induction motor, and that alteration makes it more efficient because there is less drag when it isn’t engaged. It’s more efficient at speed too. Accounting for the usual fuzzy EV-motor math, the i3 50’s full output is a meaty 463 horses and 476 pound-feet, enough to push the electric 3 to 60 mph in an estimated 4.2 seconds.

Also unlike the i4, the i3’s battery is not a limit in any way, shape, or form. It’s much more capacious, toting 112 kWh instead of the i4’s 84 kWh. We estimate the range at a fantastic 450 miles (the EPA has yet to rate it), which is a bit higher than BMW’s own number, since the electric iX3 SUV’s official range also surpassed BMW’s initial internal figure. The two vehicles share a powertrain, so we figure the powertrain’s overachieving nature will transfer from SUV to sedan too. On the charging front, the pack’s 800-volt architecture means it can gulp down electricity at 400 kilowatts (if you can find a charger that can support it). A NACS port is standard equipment, with an included adapter for SAE Combo charging.

See all results for new 2027 BMW i3 for sale near 33437

Despite leaving the optional M adaptive dampers at home, the car we drove seemed expertly tuned, with a ride that was taut but never too firm. The battery’s low mass helped keep the car feeling planted in corners, with just enough roll stiffness to keep body lean disciplined without introducing harshness or head toss to upset the proceedings.

And we pushed it hard in corners, too. Some of this feeling comes from BMW’s “Heart of Joy” computer, which sorts out the steering, friction braking, regenerative braking, throttle inputs, and more—in a claimed one-tenth of the time that previous BMW software stacks required. Brake-based rear differential action, something we usually don’t care for, was silky smooth in this system and felt for all the world like an electronically controlled rear diff. Brake response is uncommonly good, and there is enough regenerative braking capacity that nearly all your routine stops will be handled magnetically.

The one thing we were less effervescent about was the steering feel. The i3’s helm is certainly accurate and direct enough, but it doesn’t quite have the feel and feedback of the gas-powered M350 we drove (and reviewed separately). Perhaps that differentiator is there intentionally; after all, there’s a sportier i3 M60 model coming.

At least the i3 we drove didn’t have the dorky steering wheel with odd vertical spokes. (The optional M Sport wheel puts said spokes in a vastly more normal location.) BMW’s trick Panoramic Vision screen works even better in the i3 than it does in the M350, because the dash-spanning display strip is more visible above the wheel, yet it doesn’t hide the road. The taller but more steeply angled hood works in its favor, for sure. The central touchscreen is the same 17.9-inch display found in the M350 and has all the same characteristics. On the positive side, it looks great, and the angled shape is quite natural. On the other hand, let’s just say that vent aiming is better done manually, rather than via touchscreen controls, and there are other functions that could benefit from a real button or two. You can save a few bucks by not opting for the head-up display, which seems redundant when you already have a wealth of information at the base of the windscreen.

We also like the i3’s soaring panoramic glass roof, which provides an abundance of headroom. Rear-seat space is slightly larger than the M350’s, but toe space beneath the front seat can be tighter if the front occupant has their chair lowered to the floor. BMW doesn’t have a U.S.-specific figure for trunk space just yet, but preliminary German figures place its 15 cubic feet just one cube in arrears of the M350 gasser.

The BMW i3 50 xDrive will launch in the first quarter of 2027, right alongside the gas-powered 3-series lineup. It starts at $62,850, which seems like a great deal for all you get. The i3 feels mighty special and has the potential to draw new buyers into the electric fold. It’s got gobs of range, it charges fast, and it delivers speed and poise like a proper BMW.

#4497. Tesla Powerwall 3 now boosts heat pumps to store cheap solar as heat

Tesla has launched Heat Pump Optimization, a feature that lets the Powerwall 3 and three-phase Powerwall 3P tell a compatible heat pump when to run harder so a home can bank cheap or surplus solar energy as hot water.

It’s live in Europe only. Tesla hasn’t said anything about bringing it to the US or Canada, and the hardware standard it relies on barely exists on this side of the Atlantic.

According to Tesla’s support page for the feature, the Powerwall watches electricity prices and solar production throughout the day and sends the heat pump one of two signals: run normally, or boost.

When it’s told to boost, the heat pump heats water beyond what the home needs right now, typically into a domestic hot water or buffer tank. That stored heat then carries the house through the expensive hours, when the heat pump can run less.

What triggers a boost depends on the Powerwall’s operating mode:

Tesla Energy summed it up on X last week: “Heat Pump Optimization allows your Powerwall to boost heating when there’s surplus solar or energy is inexpensive.”

There’s no cloud integration with heat pump brands here. It’s a wire.

The feature runs on SG-Ready (Smart Grid Ready), a label the German Heat Pump Association (BWP) introduced back in 2012 with 17 manufacturers. It uses two relay contacts on the heat pump to signal four operating states, from a utility block to a forced switch-on. Tesla only uses the “normal” and “boosted” recommendations.

Tesla’s requirements are pretty specific:

And there are limits. The signals are only recommendations, so the heat pump’s own thermostat settings can override them. Tesla also notes each signal has to be held for at least 10 minutes to comply with SG-Ready, and the feature drops back to normal during a power outage so the Powerwall can prioritize backup loads.

Oddly, there’s no on/off toggle in the Tesla app. Once it’s wired up, it’s on.

The math is what makes this interesting. A 300-liter hot water tank heated an extra 30°C holds about 10.5 kWh of thermal energy. With a heat pump running at a COP of 3, that takes only around 3.5 kWh of electricity to store.

So a tank most European heat pump homes already have can soak up a big chunk of midday solar without touching the lithium in the garage. That leaves the Powerwall’s 13.5 kWh free for the stuff that can’t be stored as heat.

The market is there too. Germany sold 299,000 heating heat pumps in 2025, up 55% year-over-year according to BWP, and they made up nearly half of all new heating systems sold in the country for the first time.

Tesla is also late to this. sonnen pushed a software update in 2023 that lets its sonnenBatterie run heat pumps off surplus solar, starting with NIBE units, and SG-Ready control has been a standard feature of German PV energy managers for years.

watches electricity prices and solar production throughout the day and sends the heat pump one of two signals: run normally, or boost.

Heatpumps over here have been able to do this for years already.

And it's not one of two signals. Inverter controlled HP's enables control of the effect, and not just "normal or boost".

It’s the latest Europe-first move for Tesla Energy after it launched the Powerwall 3P with a native three-phase inverter earlier this year, aimed squarely at Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. The company announced its 1 millionth Powerwall last year, and software like this is how it squeezes more value out of that installed base.

This is a smart, cheap feature, and it’s exactly the kind of thing that makes a home battery more valuable without adding a single cell.

Heat is the biggest energy load in most homes in cold climates, and water is about the cheapest storage medium there is. Using a battery’s brain to time the heat pump around solar and tariffs makes a lot more sense than discharging lithium to run a compressor at 6 p.m.

Home batteries are changing the economics of residential energy, and pairing them with solar (and smart loads like heat pumps) is the best way to get the most out of them. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. #4496. Finding And Using BP Pulse EV Chargers Just Got A Whole Lot Easier

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

BP Pulse, the oil and gas giant’s EV charging subsidiary, has made it simpler for EV drivers to find and use its fast chargers across the United States.

The company’s nearly 900 DC fast chargers are now integrated into ChargeHub’s ecosystem, which claims to be the largest roaming network in North America. As a result, drivers can ditch the BP Pulse smartphone app in favor of ChargeHub’s app, which includes thousands of stalls from dozens of different operators.

Through the roaming network’s app, users can find, access, and pay for charging. The ChargeHub app also shows real-time information about available ports and their connector type. In BP Pulse’s case, roughly a third of its 874 fast chargers have a Tesla-style NACS connector, while the majority of stalls have CCS1 connectors. Some have CHAdeMO plugs.

The oil company’s chargers also have on-site credit card readers, so using an app isn’t required, but it’s helpful when trying to plan a charging stop. BP Pulse supports Plug & Charge, but it’s limited to Ford and BMW vehicles, and only the fastest stalls have the feature enabled.

Three types of chargers can be found on BP Pulse’s network. The lowest-powered stalls are made by Tritium and can deliver up to 150 kW. The company also uses 180 kW ABB dispensers, as well as 400 kW Alpitronic stalls. The smallest BP Pulse stations have just two stalls, while the largest site, located in Inglewood, California, has 48 stalls, according to DCFC Tracker. Pricing on BP Pulse varies between $0.33/kilowatt-hour and $0.65/kilowatt-hour.

"We're focused on making charging simple, reliable, and easy to access wherever drivers need it,” said Sujay Sharma, VP EV Charging at BP Pulse. “By partnering with ChargeHub, we're expanding access to the bp pulse network through trusted roaming partners for​ EV​ drivers on the road. Charging networks working better together benefits the entire EV ecosystem and is an important step toward accelerating EV adoption."

Through the ChargeHub app, drivers can find and pay for sessions at over 40 different operators in the United States and Canada. Additionally, another 70+ networks, including Tesla, Ionna, and Electrify America, can be found on ChargeHub.

#4495. Rolls-Royce Says Its Average Customer Is 43, Down from 56

Kia's Telluride Is Closing In On The Sportage's U.S. Sales Crown

Ford Crams The Most Powerful OEM Crate Engine Ever Made Into New Bronco Concept

Mercedes-Benz Wants To Blow Snow Off Your Car Before You Open The Door

Rolls-Royce has apparently lowered the average age of its customers to 43 and has even attracted Gen-Zs to its showrooms.

The Best-Selling Hyundai SUV In October Wasn’t The Tucson

Dodge Unveils Six Turnkey HEMI V8 Crate Engines With Up to 1,025 HP

Cadillac Escalade IQ Has a Suspension Squeak With No Fix Yet

This 800-HP Ford F-100 Has Mustang DNA and a $1 Million Price Tag

We want you to imagine a Rolls-Royce owner. If you pictured someone a little bit older, then we can’t blame you. The name conjures images of old-world luxury with massive estates and links to royalty. It’s either that or said owner is a captain of industry, being whisked away to important social gatherings across cities.

But while the automaker still offers traditional luxury in spades, it’s also managed to lower the average age of its buyers. As it turns out, classic luxury cars have a strong appeal for younger, affluent shoppers. The thing is, Rolls-Royce didn’t just become a brand that suddenly attracted a new era of customers, but rather, it made the effort to make it happen.

Julian Jenkins is the director of sales and brand for Rolls-Royce, and he recently told Automotive News that the average customer is 43 years old. You read that right; it’s older millennials who are now buying these cars. Before 2010, the average age was 56 years old, so how did the brand do it?

He added that, in some markets, the brand is showing relevance among the ultra-wealthy Gen-Z crowd. “In China, for example, we have some of our youngest clients who are in their mid to late 20s,” said Jenkins. There’s no doubt that China played a part in making Rolls-Royce a ‘young’ brand.

Jenkins pointed out that the Cullinan played a key role in bringing in younger customers to the marque, but it’s not the only reason for the drop in average ages. “Black Badge, Cullinan and also some of our bespoke creations have done that,” Jenkins said, further adding that it’s the ultra-exclusive Coachbuild division models such as the Boat Tail and Droptail actually attracting a younger crowd. “Those are Rolls-Royce models that have stimulated interest,” added the executive.

Rolls-Royce has since responded to the new wave of customers by transforming its showrooms. Case in point, Rolls-Royce Motor Cars Beverly Hills went from merely selling cars to a place that hosts gatherings with its speakeasy-inspired lounge and bar. It’s called the Black Badge Lounge, and before anyone dismisses it as a gimmick, it’s actually become a destination for current and prospective owners. The showroom overhaul gives the client a more immersive experience.

Rival Bentley has also adapted a similar approach when it unveiled its new look for its shops. Jack Barclay Bentley in London was the first to get the boutique treatment, and like Rolls-Royce Beverly Hills, a large part of the store is dedicated as a bar that doubles as the reception area. As for Mercedes, it’s building standalone stores for the Maybach division to provide an exclusive and unique experience that’s far elevated from the usual Mercedes-Benz showroom. The aim is to make the visit feel less transactional and more warm and welcoming.

Also, Milton Pedraza, CEO of Luxury Institute, mentioned that the baby boomers who once made up a big chunk of Rolls-Royce sales are gradually fading out. Instead of simply sticking firmly to tradition, the British automaker managed to infuse its values while tailoring it to a new generation of customers. “Rolls-Royce truly is an iconic brand. It’s one of those like Hermes: It’s been around for generations and it continues to reinvent itself. Now reinventing itself into more bespoke. You pay half a million for the base and then you spend another half a million on ‘Customize it for me,'” said Pedraza.

Of course, the brand’s customers have always wanted a more bespoke vehicle, so it’s not a generational thing. The difference now is, it’s tweaked the formula and moved with the times.

#4494. Cadillac’s most affordable EV just got a bit cheaper

The 2027 Cadillac Optiq offers up to 317 miles of range, a massive 33″ infotainment screen, an NACS charge port, and now it’s a bit more affordable.

The Optiq first went on sale in 2025 as Cadillac’s entry-level electric SUV, starting at $54,390. For the 2026 model year, the Optiq arrived as GM’s first electric vehicle with a built-in NACS port and added a new rear-wheel-drive (RWD) powertrain.

Thanks to the new RWD option, the 2026 Optiq (see our review) was also slightly less expensive, with prices starting at $52,395.

While GM initially said the 2027 Cadillac Optiq would start at $52,695, prices on its website have been updated and are now slightly lower.

The base 2027 Cadillac Optiq Luxury RWD is now listed at $51,790, or $905 less than the initial price announced months ago. The Luxury AWD trim is also $905 cheaper, starting at $55,290.

Meanwhile, the Sport trim now starts at $52,395 for RWD and $55,895 for AWD, both $900 less than before.

The higher-spec Optiq Premium Luxury, Premium Sport, and V-Series trims remain at the price GM initially announced.

The 2027 Cadillac Optiq offers up to 317 miles of range in the RWD models and 303 miles with AWD. All models come with a standard 33″ Horizon Display infotainment screen, a 19-speaker AKG Studio Audio System, GM’s Super Cruise hands-free driver-assist technology, and a native NACS charge port.

Upgrading to AWD costs an extra $3,500. The Premium Luxury and Premium Sport add standard features including a Head-Up Display, ventilated and lumbar massaging front seats, and a rear cargo cover.

The high-performance 2027 Optiq-V starts at $69,295 and delivers a Cadillac-estimated 519 lb-ft of torque and 650 horsepower in Velocity MaX Mode,

How does the Cadillac Optiq stack up against the Tesla Model Y? The base Tesla Model Y RWD starts at $39,990 with up to 321 miles of range, while the AWD version costs $41,990 and gets up to 294 miles.

The Tesla Model Y Premium RWD starts at $45,990 with up to 355 miles of range, while the Premium AWD starts at $49,990 and has 327 miles of range.

Had the opportunity to drive the Optiq as a loaner while my Lyriq was in for service. I truly liked how it handled but I did find what I call a safety issue due to its design. The A pillar has an extra vertical piece and that combined with really no usable visual space forward and the side mirror create a blind spot when wanting to make a left turn on dark roads. No problem in the city where there is light. If GM would have added front side lighting when making a turn that could have been eliminated. Would have seriously looked at the Optiq for the next vehicle but that blind spot is a show stopper for me. Well that, and the fact the Optiq does not support CarPlay.

Inside, the base Tesla Model Y has a 16″ QHD touchscreen and 7-speaker audio system. The Premium model gains a 15-speaker Tesla Audio System with a subwoofer, plus an 8″ second-row touchscreen.

The two are nearly the same size, but the Tesla Model Y offers slightly more rear legroom and cargo capacity than the Cadillac Optiq.

#4492. Nearly 1 In 3 Hyundais Sold In October Was A Hybrid As High Gas Prices Push Buyers To Pivot

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

A whopping 29% of Hyundai’s total October sales volume in the U.S. were hybrids, the automaker said Tuesday. That’s the highest mix ever for gas-electric powertrains for the Korean automaker, thanks to buyers seeking more fuel efficient cars due to gas prices that have remained stubbornly high since the start of the U.S. war in Iran.

Hyundai doesn't break out hybrid sales in its monthly reports, instead bundling them together under individual model names. But it did say that hybrid versions of the Santa Fe and Palisade set new October sales records. Meanwhile, sales of the all-electric Ioniq 5 bounced back, climbing 21% year over year to 1,981 units.

Hyundai sold 73,452 vehicles in October, a 5% increase over the same month last year. Its year-to-date sales now stand at 770,916 units, up 3% from 2025.

Sister brand Kia also reported record overall and electrified vehicle sales. It sold 80,008 vehicles last month, bringing its year-to-date total to 747,394 units, not far behind Hyundai.

Kia's hybrid sales jumped 114% year over year, helped by strong demand for hybrid versions of the popular Sportage and Sorento SUVs and the Carnival minivan. But the more interesting news is the recovery in Kia's EV sales, which have struggled for several quarters.

Sales of the three-row EV9 surged 111% to 1,406 units, while EV6 sales climbed 58% to 803 units. Kia also sold 976 units of the more affordable EV3, whose production and deliveries are still ramping up following its recent U.S. launch.

There's a caveat to those EV growth figures, though. The Ioniq 5, EV6, and EV9 were all coming off a particularly weak October 2025, when sales cratered following the expiration of the federal EV tax credit a month earlier.

The months leading up to the September 2025 deadline saw buyers rush to claim the incentive, pulling demand forward and causing subsequent sales to decline. The broader EV market has been gradually recovering since, with the third quarter marking its strongest performance since then.

The EV3, meanwhile, could give Kia's electric lineup another shot in the arm. Starting at $31,385 including destination, it's among the cheapest EVs on sale in the U.S., alongside the Nissan Leaf and Chevrolet Bolt. We recently reviewed the small electric crossover and think it offers really good value.

Hyundai could also see another boost to its EV business in the coming months. The automaker is preparing to supply Waymo with tens of thousands of Ioniq 5-based robotaxis, Hyundai CEO José Muñoz said in September. That could be a new source of demand for its electric crossover, beyond individual consumers.

#4490. Hardee’s gets EV fast charging – with Carl’s Jr. locations to follow

EV drivers have a new reason to pull into Hardee’s. Energized EV has opened four fast-charging ports at a restaurant in Temple, Georgia, kicking off a planned rollout at Hardee’s and Carl’s Jr. locations across the US.

There’s no site count or rollout schedule yet, but the first location is open with both NACS and CCS1 connectors.

The chargers are at 587 Carrollton Street in Temple. The site has two dual-port XCharge C7 DC fast chargers, each rated at 240 kW, for a total of four charging ports. Monta provides the chargers’ software. XCharge says the C7 adjusts power output between its two connectors, and both NACS and CCS1 connectors are on offer.

“Adding charging at our restaurants gives EV drivers a convenient place to stop, recharge, and enjoy a meal,” said Mike Darger, vice president of facilities and maintenance at CKE Restaurants. “We look forward to building on this first opening as more locations come online across the country.”

Energized EV says more Hardee’s and Carl’s Jr. sites are planned across the US, with president and CEO Devin Grandis calling Temple “the beginning of a much larger expansion.”

Energy & Environmental Design Services LLC (E&EDS) is the program’s exclusive installer. Its services include charging infrastructure design, installation, and maintenance, as well as electrical contracting.

Yes. I love this. As in past comments sections on stories like this, the question comes up for me as to how they manage them. Will people eating there use them or will they become a "charging stop" that drivers use often? Then there's the saga of how to keep the lazy and over-sized patrons from parking their 2004 Explorer in those spaces.

Gas stations with food offered and restaurants with charging offered are similar yet different. Instead of eating while you gas up, we can now charge up while we eat. The latter being the better option.

Energized EV’s approach is to install chargers where drivers already stop, whether they’re running errands or taking a longer road trip. But we’ll need the next locations and opening dates to see how useful this restaurant charging network will become. The announcement doesn’t list charging prices for Temple.

The Chevrolet Trax is arriving for the 2027 model year with a mid-cycle update, adding new features inside and out while streamlining the trim range from five to three. Full specifications haven’t been disclosed yet, but apparently, the engine has been updated as well.

According to GM Authority, the upcoming Trax will retain the same 1.2-liter turbocharged three-cylinder engine, but will produce 140 horsepower and 162 lb-ft of torque. That’s a three-horsepower increase over the outgoing model, while the torque figure remains unchanged. However, peak torque now arrives at 4,000 rpm instead of 2,500 rpm.

Judging how the reported engine tuning changes will affect the driving experience is difficult, especially since the full torque curve isn’t available. But generally, because peak torque arrives later, the engine may need to rev higher to deliver its maximum pulling power, potentially affecting acceleration at lower speeds. If this results in gentler, less abrupt acceleration, it could improve passenger comfort, potentially a welcome change for a vehicle primarily used as a daily driver.

The Trax retains a 6-speed automatic transmission and front-wheel drive across all trims. All-wheel drive remains unavailable, but on the bright side, sticking with FWD helps keep costs down.

Arguably, the reported engine changes won’t be as significant as the other updates, particularly the new connectivity features and vehicle electronics. There’s also a larger 11.3-inch touchscreen with Google built-in and an 11-inch digital instrument cluster, updates that would likely be more meaningful to mainstream buyers. Still, some may appreciate knowing the ins and outs of the 2027 model.

This mid-cycle update comes at a time when the Trax is selling well in the U.S. The subcompact crossover sold 206,339 units in 2025, up 2.8% compared to the previous year and marking its best annual sales ever. It also sold 57,917 units in Q3 2026, up 16.3% year over year. As such, Chevrolet is refreshing an already popular vehicle rather than attempting to revive a struggling nameplate. With the Malibu discontinued, the Trax stands as the brand’s most affordable model.

The Trax is still sourced from General Motors’ Changwon plant in South Korea, leaving it exposed to U.S. import tariffs. The 2027 model will be offered in three trims: LT, RS, and Activ, but pricing has yet to be announced.

#4487. The BMW iX is sold out, but you might like what takes its place even more

BMW is saying goodbye to the iX. With the 2026 model essentially sold out, BMW is preparing to introduce its replacement, which already looks like a big upgrade.

The iX went on sale in the US in 2022 as BMW’s first dedicated electric SUV. After a short four-year run, BMW confirmed earlier this year that it was discontinuing the iX in the US after the 2026 model year to make room for its next-generation of fully electric vehicles.

BMW didn’t take long to sell through inventory, with 2026 iX models essentially sold out in the US.

The iX landing page now redirects you to the new BMW X5 instead. According to online auto research firm CarsDirect, about 10 new iX models remain nationwide.

BMW’s Neue Klasse vehicles, starting with the new 2027 iX3, mark a step change from its previous EVs.

At the center is the Neue Klasse platform, which introduces BMW’s sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive, new batteries, and an 800-volt electrical architecture.

BMW said the new Gen6 eDrive system delivers 30% higher charging speeds and driving range than its previous system, with some models seeing an even greater increase.

The 2027 iX3 50 xDrive, BMW’s first Neue Klasse vehicle, starts at $61,500 and offers an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 434 miles. In comparison, the 2026 iX xDrive 60 had an EPA range of up to 364 miles.

While the iX3 is a smaller, compact electric SUV compared to the iX, BMW is preparing to launch the iX5 as a more direct replacement.

The gas-powered 2027 X5 40 xDrive is now on sale, starting at $72,100, but BMW is expected to launch the electric iX5 in early 2027.

A few weeks ago, BMW put the new iX5 60 xDrive to the test at an international media event in Southern California to show just how fast it can charge.

During the event, the new iX5 hit a peak of 464 kW. BMW said that with up to 460 kW peak charging, the iX5 60 xDrive can add up to 170 miles of range in 10 minutes. To charge the battery from 10% to 80% takes just 22 minutes.

Using a 144 kWh battery, BMW said the electric SUV will offer up to an estimated 435 miles of range on a single charge.

The iX5 is powered by a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain, delivering a combined 578 hp (425 kW) and 593 lb-ft of torque. BMW says it can go from 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds and tow up to 6,000 lbs.

Inside, the iX5 will be an upgrade from the iX, adopting BMW’s Neue Klasse design. The setup includes a 17.9″ navigation touchscreen and the new BMW Panoramic Vision that spans the windshield. You can also opt to add the optional 14.6″ passenger screen for a third display.

The new drive platform is a huge improvement. Personally I'm glad to see it in the new i3 since I don't think everyone needs a 3-ton SUV.

Measuring 197.2″ long, 78.7″ wide, and 68.9″ tall, the iX5 is slightly longer and taller than the outgoing iX, with more of a traditional SUV design.

BMW is expected to open orders for the new iX5 60 xDrive this month, starting at $79,800, with a full launch in early 2027. It will be BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US.

Production is set to begin at BMW’s Plant Spartanburg in South Carolina by the end of the year, with the first deliveries expected in early 2027.

#4486. Defying Online Backlash, The Ferrari Luce EV Is Already Sold Out Through 2027

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Ferrari's first all-electric model is already sold out for 2027, the automaker said during its third-quarter earnings call Tuesday. The Luce starts at an eye-watering $560,800 in the U.S., but neither its price nor its controversial design appears to be putting off Ferrari's deep-pocketed clientele.

“The Luce that we plan to sell next year basically are all allocated,” Ferrari CEO Benedetto Vigna said in the earnings call. He added that customers placing an order now would have to wait a year to take delivery. Ferrari didn't disclose how many units it plans to sell or provide a regional breakdown of its orders.

Designed through a collaboration with former Apple design chief Jony Ive's LoveFrom, the first electric Prancing Horse looks nothing like the Ferraris we're used to seeing. It trades the brand's signature aggressive, low-slung proportions for a higher-riding silhouette with an industrial-design aesthetic. The Luce is also Ferrari's first-ever five-seat car. The radical departure hasn't gone down particularly well with critics, many of whom have questioned whether the design looks like a Ferrari at all.

Ferrari isn't alone in taking a more unconventional approach to EV design. Jaguar's new Type 01 and the all-electric Mercedes-AMG GT have also sparked plenty of debate. Key rival Lamborghini, meanwhile, has scrapped plans for its first-ever EV, opting to stick with hybrids and gas models for now.

Vigna, however, said buyers were better understanding the Luce after seeing it in person and getting behind the wheel. “We see when and how the perception changes when the people drive the car,” he said.

Early media reviews appear to support that argument. A handful of outlets have already had the opportunity to drive the Luce, and the initial impressions have been overwhelmingly positive. MotorTrend, for instance, described its driving dynamics as “beguilingly natural in its responses, fluid and concise in its change of direction, and beautifully balanced through all phases of a corner.”

The Luce is a beast on paper. It's equipped with quad motors—one at each wheel—for a total of 1,035 horsepower and 730 pound-feet of torque. That's enough to rocket the Luce to 62 mph in 2.5 seconds, Ferrari says. The EV also has rear-wheel steering and a suspension setup derived from the F80 supercar. Steering wheel-mounted paddles let the driver jack up torque or regenerative braking, which is supposed to make the car more engaging to drive.

The EV-specific specs are less impressive for a half-million-dollar car. The Luce's 112-kilowatt-hour battery uses SK On pouch cells and provides 530 kilometers (329 miles) of range on Europe's WLTP cycle. That should translate to somewhere under 300 miles when it gets an EPA rating. Peak charging power lands at 350 kilowatts, which is plenty strong in objective terms but falls short of some of the fastest-charging EVs. But then again, you don't buy a $560,000 Luce because you're looking for a great, practical electric car.

And if there were any doubts about how much wealthy collectors are willing to pay for Ferrari's first EV, consider what happened in August. The first production Luce, dubbed “Chassis 0,” fetched a staggering $40 million at auction, making it the most expensive new car ever sold at auction.

Ford has been hyping up its affordable EV truck lately. We all know it’ll be called the Fathom, and the prototype has been spotted multiple times already. Ford has even released ‘official spy shots’ of the battery-powered pickup, getting buzz going as early as now.

The Fathom is scheduled to make its world premiere during the second half of 2027, with preorders opening early next year. Ford has even launched a teaser website showing off some features that we may see in the production model.

Per the Detroit Free Press, Ford CEO Jim Farley gave some hints on what we could expect from the Fathom. During a Wall Street analysts call, Farley said “It completely blew me away. Zero to 60 is huge … and the hands free experience was like something I’ve never experienced. Fathom is really a breakthrough product. It’s highly capable, innovative, affordable.”

Farley also reiterated the price of the Fathom, promising it’ll start under $30,000. Should Ford be able to keep the promise of a sub-$30,000 base price, the Fathom will have a price spread of about $10,000. That leaves a lot of room for trims to be made, along with other options. Either way, it will be interesting to see how Ford will structure the model lineup, given that it’s gunning for EV owners looking for more utility, as well as conquest sales from hybrids and pure combustion vehicle owners. The fact that the company aims to make the entire Fathom lineup go for under $40,000 is a bold and ambitious move, but it should help the company see more success in the EV market.

Frick says they expect the Fathom “to attract new and used EV buyers, but also (gasoline) and hybrid customers, especially because we’re going to have much lower operating costs than even a mainstream hybrid vehicle.”

The pickup rides on the UEV architecture, and it’s also known as the Universal Electric Vehicle platform. It’s a clean-sheet design developed by a skunkworks team based in Long Beach, California. Ford needs the Fathom to be a great success, especially since the company invested greatly in to the new chassis. Should it be able to do that, it has the potential to spawn more models from the UEV platform, such as affordable EV crossovers and sedans, and hopefully banish memories of the F-150 Lightning’s slow sales.

#4484. Shaquille O’Neal Bought This 2004 Rolls-Royce Phantom Just to Prove a Point

It’s now for sale on Bring a Trailer. Maybe you’ve got something to prove?

One of the greatest basketball players of all time, four-time NBA champion Shaquille O’Neal was one of the most formidable centers in the game. That doesn’t mean he never got outplayed.

To hear him tell the story, during his stint playing for the Lakers, he wandered into a Rolls-Royce dealership dressed casually in sweats. In his words, “I like to spend money, but I don’t like to waste money. I don’t want to spend $400,000 for a car.” Thus, every time the salesman tells him the price for a particular Roller, O'Neal waves him off.

Finally, the salesman asks, “You’re asking about all these cars—can you afford them?” Riled up, Shaq buys three Rolls-Royces on the spot. Heck of a flex by the NBA player, but not a bad move by the salesman, who gets to pocket a triple-Rolls commission.

See all results for used cars for sale near 21014

One of that trio of Rolls-Royces just turned up at Bring a Trailer (which, like Car and Driver, is part of Hearst Autos): a 2004 Phantom sedan in glossy silver. Yes, the driver’s seat goes back, way back, but this Roller is going to set you back far less than O’Neal’s impulse purchase.

This was the debut model year for the Phantom VII, the first Rolls-Royce of the BMW ownership era. Like Shaq, much of this generation of Rolls-Royce’s curb presence comes from its sheer size; the sedan was longer than a Ford Excursion when it launched.

Power came from an enlarged version of the BMW 750’s V-12, here displacing 6.75 liters. Peak power was 453 horsepower, but a more subtle motivating force was the 531 pound-feet of torque. Almost 400 pound-feet was available from just 1000 rpm, fed through a smooth-shifting six-speed automatic, giving the Phantom a driving experience less like a luxury sedan and more like a Cunard cruise liner.

Add in coach doors with integrated umbrellas, self-righting Rolls-Royce center-caps on the wheels, and a retractable Spirit of Ecstasy on the massive hood, and this generation of Phantom is plenty imposing. It’s even better on the inside, with acres of walnut trim, buttery leather, and deep-pile lambswool carpets. Other faintly ridiculous amenities include rear picnic tables and six-zone climate control.

Shaq says he barely drove his three Rolls-Royces, although this example now has 45K miles on the odometer. That means there’s still plenty of luxurious life ahead, along with a great story about the day somebody scored on Shaquille O’Neal.

#4483. bp pulse makes 850+ EV fast chargers easier to use in the US

EV drivers have another way to charge at bp pulse without adding its app to their phones. The network has joined ChargeHub’s Passport Hub, connecting more than 850 charging points at over 95 US locations to ChargeHub and participating charging services and automakers.

Drivers can find, access, and pay for bp pulse charging through ChargeHub or participating services connected to Passport Hub.

Passport Hub handles the connections between charging networks and the services drivers use, including exchanging session information and settling payments. That lets a charging operator connect to multiple services through a single integration.

In practice, ChargeHub users can pull up a bp pulse location, select a port, and start charging from their existing account. The app displays the charging cost and wallet balance, and drivers need funds in their ChargeHub wallet to begin charging.

ChargeHub also shows real-time charger availability and lets drivers filter by connector type. Its bp pulse guide says most of the network’s chargers use CCS, with a growing share offering NACS.

Meanwhile, bp pulse has been adding physical charging sites, too. Recent openings include 12 charging bays at a TravelCenters of America location in Grand Bay, Alabama, and 22 bays near Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport.

Before starting a session, check the price shown in the app. ChargeHub’s guide notes that its Plus subscription waives activation fees, so using an existing account doesn’t necessarily mean paying the same total as another payment method.

#4482. Used EVs Are Selling Like Hotcakes. The Fastest Movers May Surprise You

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Used EVs are getting more popular. Not only are they increasing in popularity, they're selling even faster than their hybrid and even gasoline counterparts, according to iSeeCars.

You might assumed that all of the used Teslas hitting the market would be a big reason why. But in reality, no Tesla even cracked the top 10 list of best-selling used EVs in September 2026.

Compared to the same month last year, this September saw a 9.8% price increase for used EVs. That's exactly double the 4.8% increase used hybrids saw year-over-year. However, both absolutely crush used gas car values, which only jumped 0.3%. You can bet that high fuel prices over the past year or so have had an affect on gas and diesel demand. People are thinking about EVs more than ever before, especially every time the see eye-watering receipts from every fill up.

“These pricing shifts reflect significantly different year-over-year trends across drivetrains,” iSeeCars Executive Analyst Karl Brauer said in a release. “Ongoing higher fuel prices are likely driving the shift, though the EV segment has also recovered from the demand turbulence caused by the loss of federal incentives a year ago.”

Price isn't the only indicator of demand, though. Speed is another. Used EVs fly off the figurative shelves faster than gas cars, spending an average of 41.9 days on the lot. Not only is that 10.1% faster than September 2025, but it's almost two weeks faster on average than gas cars, which take 54.8 days to sell. Furthermore, gas car sale time increased by 19.9%. So it's getting harder to sell used gas cars, while EVs are getting easier.

Admittedly, in defense of gas cars, customers are spoiled for choice. There are far, far more gas cars available for sale—for example, Autotrader lists 1,384,383 used gas and diesel cars nationwide, but only 44,434 used EVs. There are also fewer EV models for sale, so customers aren't cross-shopping as much. Still, there's no denying that used EV demand is increasing as supply continues to grow.

There are also more options than ever in a market that was once essentially wholly dominated by Tesla. But in September, none of the top 10 fastest-selling used EV models were Teslas. There weren't any Lucids or Rivians in there, either. The quickest-selling EVs were oddly the Audi Q4 E-tron Sportback, followed by the Toyota bZX4, and Lexus RZ 300e. So it seems that used EV customers are becoming like everyone else: they just want something small and practical, with some quirky styling and a nice interior. Also on the list were the Honda Prologue, BMW iX, and even Polestar 2.

The slowest-selling EVs aren't exactly surprising, though, as they're mostly massive and expensive SUVs and trucks. The Cadillac Escalade IQ was the slowest-seller by a huge margin, but it's also uber-expensive. It was followed by the GMC Sierra EV, Chevy Silverado EV, and the Volvo EX90. The Hummer EV was on the list, too, proving that GM's Ultium trucks aren't exactly popular on the used market.

One of the reasons why used Teslas might not have sold as quickly as other EVs is that their prices have increased. The Tesla Model S and Model X both saw used price increases of 22% and 18%, respectively. That is good for the two highest of any used car on the market, regardless of powertrain.

It's interesting to see used EVs increasing in selling speed, showing that customers are willing to go electric when the vehicle type and price suits their needs. And now that data has come out proving that EVs don't lose as much range over time as previously thought, it seems that used EVs are becoming better and better buys.

#4481. Yamaha unveils new NMAX E, bringing electric power to its popular motorbike lineup

Yamaha is expanding its electric two-wheeler lineup with a much more capable machine, unveiling the new NMAX E as an electric version of its popular NMAX sport scooter.

The 2027 Yamaha NMAX E is being positioned as a 125cc-equivalent electric scooter, putting it firmly above the low-speed urban electric scooters that have made up much of Yamaha’s electric lineup thus far.

At its heart is Yamaha’s new compact eAxle drive unit, which sends power to the rear wheel through a belt drive. The electric motor produces 6.7 kW (9 hp) of nominal power and peaks at 7.5 kW (10 hp), along with 33.3 Nm (24.6 lb-ft) of torque.

Yamaha hasn’t published a top speed in the specifications, but the NMAX E’s A1 classification puts it in the same general category as 125cc combustion scooters rather than urban mopeds.

Power comes from a centrally mounted 3.5 kWh lithium-ion battery, which Yamaha says provides up to 104 km (65 miles) of range on the WMTC Class 1 testing cycle. The L-shaped battery is mounted low and centrally in the chassis to help maintain a low center of gravity.

Unlike many electric scooters that rely on removable batteries, the NMAX E uses a fixed pack. Yamaha has compensated for that with an onboard 800W charger, allowing riders to plug the scooter directly into a household outlet or an AC Type 2 public charging station. A full 0-100% charge takes around 5.5 hours.

Riders can choose between three riding modes. Sport (S) mode offers the quickest acceleration, Touring (T) provides smoother power delivery for everyday riding and carrying a passenger, and Eco (E) reduces acceleration and top speed while maximizing range. Regenerative braking is also included.

The rest of the scooter is fairly well equipped, including traction control, ABS, 245mm front and rear disc brakes, 13-inch wheels, a 33mm fork, dual rear shocks, and even a reverse mode to make low-speed maneuvering easier.

Nice, the Nmax has always been the premium scoot we try to get when traveling in southeast asia. Always felt like it would've been even better electrified. No removable battery seems a bit of a miss. That might constrain a big chunk of demand.

A five-inch TFT display includes smartphone connectivity through Yamaha’s Motor On app, providing turn-by-turn navigation as well as battery status, ride information, maintenance reminders, and other connected features. There’s also keyless ignition, USB-C charging, LED lighting, and illuminated underseat storage large enough for a full-face helmet, depending on its size.

Perhaps most importantly, the NMAX E looks like a proper Yamaha scooter rather than an electric experiment. Its dual headlights and distinctive side panels closely follow the styling language of Yamaha’s existing MAX family.

That could prove important as established motorcycle manufacturers increasingly attempt to bring electric models into their existing lineups rather than treating them as separate curiosities.

Pricing and exact market availability haven’t yet been announced, but Yamaha is positioning the NMAX E as a 2027 model for the European market.

FTC: We use income earning auto affiliate links. More.

Micah Toll is a personal electric vehicle enthusiast, battery nerd, and author of the Amazon #1 bestselling books DIY Lithium Batteries, DIY Solar Power, The Ultimate DIY Ebike Guide and The Electric Bike Manifesto.

The e-bikes that make up Micah’s current daily drivers are the $999 Lectric XP 2.0, the $1,095 Ride1Up Roadster V2, the $1,199 Rad Power Bikes RadMission, and the $3,299 Priority Current. But it’s a pretty evolving list these days.

You can send Micah tips at Micah@electrek.co, or find him on Twitter, Instagram, or TikTok.
